+title: ".clineignore (deprecated)"

+description: "Cline no longer applies .clineignore on its own. Use a hook to block access to the files it lists."
 ---
 
 <Warning>
-  **`.clineignore` will be deprecated soon.**
+  **Cline no longer reads `.clineignore` on its own.**
 
-  `.clineignore` filters what Cline loads automatically, but it is not a security or access-control boundary — ignored files can still be read via explicit `@` mentions or shell commands. We're moving away from it as a supported feature.
+  The VS Code extension stopped applying `.clineignore` in version 4.0, and the CLI and Cline Desktop never applied it. A `.clineignore` file now does nothing unless you add the hook below. See [Deprecations](/resources/deprecations#clineignore).

Let's remove this documentation entirely now that .clineignore is no longer supported anywhere.

I think we should remove the filter as well, because it isn't effective: The model can just `cat` these files and read them anyway.

---
 title: "Hooks"
 sidebarTitle: "Hooks"
-description: "See details under SDK Plugins page."
+description: "Run your own scripts when Cline starts a task, calls a tool, or finishes, and block or adjust what it does."
 ---
 
-See details under [SDK Plugins](/sdk/plugins).
\ No newline at end of file
+A hook is a script that Cline runs at a point in a task, such as before every tool call. Cline sends the script a JSON description of the event on stdin. For some events, the script can reply on stdout to stop the task or to give the model more context.
+
+Hooks work in the CLI, Cline Desktop and the VS Code extension. To run your own code inside Cline instead of a separate script, write a [plugin](/sdk/plugins), whose runtime hooks such as `beforeTool` are typed functions.
+
+## Where Hooks Live
+
+A hook is a file named after its event, such as `PreToolUse.sh`, in a hooks folder:
+
+| Folder | CLI and Desktop | VS Code extension |
+|--------|-----------------|-------------------|
+| `.cline/hooks/` in the workspace | Yes | No |
+| `.clinerules/hooks/` in the workspace | Yes | Yes |
+| `~/.cline/hooks/` | Yes | No |
+| `~/Documents/Cline/Hooks/` | Yes | Yes |
+
+Cline runs every matching hook it finds, from all of these folders. To see which hooks the CLI finds, run `cline config hooks`. `--config` and `CLINE_DIR` move `~/.cline/hooks/` but not `~/Documents/Cline/Hooks/`.
+
+## Hook Events
+
+Cline runs a hook each time its event happens. Each message you send starts a new run, so `TaskStart` and `TaskComplete` run once per message, not once per conversation.
+
+| File name | Runs | CLI and Desktop | VS Code extension |
+|-----------|------|-----------------|-------------------|
+| `TaskStart` | When Cline starts work on a message | Yes | Yes |
+| `TaskResume` | In place of `TaskStart`, when you resume a session in the CLI | CLI only | No |
+| `UserPromptSubmit` | When you send a message | No (see [Known Problems](#known-problems)) | Yes |
+| `PreToolUse` | Before each tool call | Yes | Yes |
+| `PostToolUse` | After each tool call | Yes | Yes |
+| `TaskComplete` | When Cline finishes replying to a message | Yes | Yes |
+| `TaskError` | When a run fails with an error | Yes | No |
+| `TaskCancel` | When you cancel a run | No (see [Known Problems](#known-problems)) | Yes |
+| `SessionShutdown` | When you cancel a run | Yes | No |
+
+The CLI and Desktop also accept `PreCompact` as a file name but never run it.
+
+## File Names and Languages
+
+In the CLI and Desktop, the name can have no extension or one of `.sh`, `.bash`, `.zsh`, `.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.ts`, `.mts`, `.cts`, `.py` or `.ps1`. A script with a `#!` line runs with that interpreter. Otherwise Cline picks one from the extension: `bash` for shell scripts and files with no extension, `node` for JavaScript, `bun run` for TypeScript, `python3` (or `py -3` on Windows) for Python, and PowerShell for `.ps1`.
+
+The VS Code extension looks for one file per event. On macOS and Linux it is the name with no extension, such as `PreToolUse`, and must be executable (`chmod +x`). On Windows it is `<Name>.ps1`, such as `PreToolUse.ps1`.
+
+## What a Hook Receives
+
+Each hook gets one JSON object on stdin. Every event includes `hookName`, `taskId`, `timestamp` and `workspaceRoots`. In the VS Code extension, `hookName` is the file name, such as `PreToolUse`. The CLI and Desktop use their own names: `agent_start`, `agent_resume`, `prompt_submit`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `agent_end`, `agent_error`, `agent_abort` and `session_shutdown`, in the order of the table above. In the CLI and Desktop, a `PreToolUse` hook also gets the call:
+
+```json
+{
+  "hookName": "tool_call",
+  "taskId": "conv-123",
+  "workspaceRoots": ["/path/to/repo"],
+  "tool_call": {
+    "id": "call-456",
+    "name": "read_files",
+    "input": { "files": [{ "path": "src/index.ts" }] }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+The VS Code extension sends the call as `preToolUse.toolName` and `preToolUse.parameters` instead. The [`.clineignore` hook](/customization/clineignore#the-hook-script) shows a script that reads both shapes.
+
+## What a Hook Can Do
+
+A hook that only watches can print `{}`. To act, print one JSON object:
+
+| Field | Effect |
+|-------|--------|
+| `cancel` | `true` stops the task. Send a new message to continue. |
+| `errorMessage` | The reason shown when `cancel` is `true`. |
+| `contextModification` | Text added for the model to read on its next request. The CLI and Desktop also accept the name `context`. |
+| `overrideInput` | Replaces the tool call's input. `PreToolUse` in the CLI and Desktop only. |
+
+Only some events read the reply:
+
+- **CLI and Desktop:** `PreToolUse` and `PostToolUse` hooks can stop the task or add context. Cline waits up to 2 minutes for each one. Hooks for the other events start and run on their own while Cline carries on, and Cline doesn't read their reply.
+- **VS Code extension:** `TaskStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse` and `PostToolUse` hooks can stop the task or add context. Cline waits up to 30 seconds for every hook, including `TaskComplete` and `TaskCancel`, whose reply it ignores.
+
+Write logs to stderr. Cline reads stdout as the hook's reply.
+
+Hooks don't run for tools that the model provider runs itself. With the Claude Code and OpenAI Codex CLI providers, `PreToolUse` and `PostToolUse` never run.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
In cases like this, I would rather clean up the product and delete the line from the documentation. Or fix the product and keep it.

Reason is, it looks silly to document something that does nothing. Why did we document this thing that does nothing, and not other things?

It would be different if we indicated it does X, caveat, it is broken right now. That implies it WILL do that thing again soon...

TBH if something was broken enough for us not to notice for a long time, and isn't a core part of the product, it is probably a good sign we should remove it. I am OK if you nominate some PRs you want fixed in a certain direction and block landing the doc update on those PRs resolving. Only exception is cases where that's a ton of complicated work, in that case, we have to keep moving forward and we should document the caveats and fix them asynchronously. This is presumably not that scale of issue.)

### `auth [options] [provider]`
 
-Configure authentication with an AI provider.
+Configure authentication with an AI provider. Without options, `cline auth` opens an interactive setup. To set up without prompts, pass the provider, key and model:
 
 ```bash
 cline auth
+cline auth -p anthropic -k "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" -m claude-sonnet-4-6
 ```
 
-### `config [options]`
+| Option | Description |
+|--------|-------------|
+| `-p, --provider <id>` | Provider ID (or pass it as the first argument) |
+| `-k, --apikey <key>` | API key |
+| `-m, --modelid <id>` | Model ID |
+| `-b, --baseurl <url>` | Base URL |
+| `--azure-api-version <version>` | Azure API version |
+
+### `config [options] [target]`
 
-Show current configuration.
+In a terminal, `cline config` opens the configuration view. Name a target to print one part of the configuration instead: `workflows`, `rules`, `skills`, `agents`, `plugins`, `hooks`, `mcp` or `tools`.
 
 ```bash
 cline config
+cline config mcp
+cline config tools --json
 ```
 
-### `connect [options] [adapter]`
+| Option | Description |
+|--------|-------------|
+| `--json` | Print the target as JSON |
 
-Connect to messaging platforms. See [Connectors](/cli/connectors).
+### `connect [options] [channel]`
+
+Connect Cline to a messaging channel: `telegram`, `slack`, `discord`, `gchat`, `whatsapp` or `linear`. Without a channel, `cline connect` opens a setup wizard. See [Connectors](/cli/connectors).
 
 ```bash
 cline connect
-cline connect [adapter]
+cline connect telegram -k <BOT-TOKEN>
+cline connect telegram --help    # Options for one channel
 ```
 
+| Option | Description |
+|--------|-------------|
+| `--stop` | Stop every connector, or only the named channel's |
+| `--restart` | Restart the named channel's connector. Pass the same options you started it with |
+
 ### `mcp`
 
-Manage MCP servers. See [MCP](/mcp/mcp-overview).
+Manage MCP servers. In a terminal, `cline mcp` opens a menu to list, add, edit, enable or disable, authorize and delete servers. See [MCP](/mcp/mcp-overview).
 
 ```bash
 cline mcp
+cline mcp add files --yes -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem .
+cline mcp add docs https://example.com/mcp --transport http --header "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" --yes
+cline mcp remove docs
 ```
 
-### `dev`
-
-Developer tools and utilities.
-
-```bash
-cline dev
-```
+`cline mcp add` (or `install`) saves a server: a command and its arguments after `--` for a local server, or a URL for a remote one. Without `--yes`, it opens the add wizard with those fields filled in. `cline mcp remove` (or `uninstall`) deletes a server by name.
 
 ### `doctor`
 
 Diagnose and fix configuration issues.
 
 ```bash
 cline doctor
+cline doctor fix    # Kill all running Cline processes
+cline doctor log    # Open the CLI log file
 ```
 
 ### `history|h [options]`
 
-List session history or manage saved sessions.
+List session history or manage saved sessions. In a terminal, `cline history` opens a session picker; otherwise it prints the list.
 
 ```bash
 cline history
-cline h
+cline history --json --limit 10
+cline history export <session-id> -o session.html
+cline history delete --session-id <session-id>
 ```
 
+| Option or command | Description |
+|--------|-------------|
+| `--json` | Print the sessions as JSON |
+| `--limit <count>` | Maximum number of sessions to show (default: `50`) |
+| `--page <number>` | Page of results to show |

## JSON Output Format
 
-When using `--json`, each message is a JSON object on its own line:
+With `--json`, the CLI prints one JSON object per line. Every line has a `type` and a `ts` (an ISO 8601 timestamp):
 
 ```json
-{"type": "say", "text": "I'll create the file now.", "ts": 1760501486669, "say": "text"}
+{"ts":"2026-10-07T04:49:43.041Z","type":"agent_event","event":{"type":"done","reason":"completed","text":"Hello!","iterations":1}}
 ```
 
-| Field | Type | Description |
-|-------|------|-------------|
-| `type` | `"ask"` or `"say"` | Message category |
-| `text` | `string` | Message content |
-| `ts` | `number` | Unix timestamp in milliseconds |
-| `say` | `string` | Subtype when `type` is `"say"` |
-| `ask` | `string` | Subtype when `type` is `"ask"` |
-| `reasoning` | `string` | Model reasoning (if available) |
-| `partial` | `boolean` | `true` while streaming |
+| `type` | Description |
+|--------|-------------|
+| `agent_event` | An event from the agent, in `event`. `event.type` is one of the [agent events](/sdk/reference/events#agentevent): `content_start`, `content_update`, `content_end`, `iteration_start`, `iteration_end`, `usage`, `notice`, `done` or `error` |
+| `hook_event` | A lifecycle hook ran (`hookEventName`, `agentId`, `taskId`) |
+| `team_event` | An event from an [agent team](/cli/agent-teams), in `event` |
+| `run_result` | The run finished: `finishReason`, `iterations`, `usage`, `durationMs`, `model` and the final `text` |
+| `run_aborted` | Follows `run_result` when the run was stopped (`reason`, `message`) |
